title: Count Pairs in Two Arrays
summary: For two integer arrays nums1 and nums2 of equal length n, calculate the count of index pairs (i, j) where i is less than j and the sum of nums1[i] and nums1[j] exceeds the sum of nums2[i] and nums2[j].
statement: For two integer arrays nums1 and nums2 of equal length n, calculate the count of index pairs (i, j) where i is less than j and the sum of nums1[i] and nums1[j] exceeds the sum of nums2[i] and nums2[j]. Return the total count of such pairs.
constraints: The arrays have equal length from 1 through 100000.
Count i < j only when nums1[i]+nums1[j] is strictly greater than nums2[i]+nums2[j].
hints: Move all terms to one side: a pair qualifies when two values of nums1[i]-nums2[i] sum above zero.
Sort those differences and inspect the smallest and largest remaining values.
If their sum is positive, the largest pairs with every remaining value; otherwise discard the smallest.
Sorted order makes each bulk count or discard safe, so every qualifying pair is counted exactly once.
editorial: Sorted order makes each bulk count or discard safe, so every qualifying pair is counted exactly once.

tests.explanation: Only the two indices with positive difference form a strictly positive pair sum, so the answer is one.
The transformed differences [0,6,5,-3] contain four positive-sum index pairs.
